title: Surgical unwind - artifact gap notes
content:
Context:
We detected canary degradation after the 2026-03-10 midnight deploy of web-service:v2.14.0 -> symptoms were increased p95 latency and 502 spikes only on canary nodes (5% traffic). The rollout was halted by CI webhook but some pods had already pulled the new image. This is a living scratchpad of commands tried, short error snippets, hypotheses and the minimal surgical unwind steps to get canary back to correct behavior without full cluster revert.

High-level hypothesis: some models/weights referenced by the service were built into the artifact but rely on a config change that was not flipped, causing heavy cold-start and KV cache thrash on GPU backends. Another possibility: image digest mismatch between registry and cluster due to tag-force-repush (same tag moved).

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-03-10 00:00 UTC: Buildkite bk/infra/7421 produced web-service:2.14.0, built from commit 0f3a4b2 (git sha).
- 2026-03-10 00:10 UTC: Canary rollout (5%) started via helm chart release web-svc-frontend v3.2.
- 2026-03-10 00:18 UTC: Increased p95 and 502s observed on canary only (Grafana alert).
- 2026-03-10 00:22 UTC: Traffic routing paused, but 3 of 6 canary pods already restarted with new image.
- 2026-03-10 00:33 UTC: SRE put canary to 0% traffic. Telemetry shows persistent crashloops on 2 pods until they were evicted.

Commands attempted (notes inline):
- Check image used by ReplicaSet: 
  kubectl -n prod get rs -l app=web-service -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.template.spec.containers[*].image}'
  -> output: gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service:2.14.0 gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service:2.13.2
  (weird: two images because stable RS still present)

- Inspect pod env + image digest: 
  kubectl -n prod describe pod web-service-canary-5f6d8 | egrep 'Image:|Image ID:|Args:|Events:' -A2
  -> Image: gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service:2.14.0
  -> Image ID: gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service@sha256:9b7c2d...
  -> Events: Back-off restarting failed container

- Pull locally to compare layers (from bastion):
  docker pull gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service:2.14.0
  docker inspect gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service:2.14.0 --format '{{.Id}}'
  -> local id: sha256:9b7c2d... (matches cluster Image ID)

- Check registry tag history (GCR rewrite suspicion):
  gcloud container images describe gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service:2.14.0 --show-package-vulnerabilities
  -> no retag history available (GCR doesn't show moved tags)

- Grep for model files expected at /opt/models/:
  kubectl -n prod exec -it web-service-canary-5f6d8 -- ls -la /opt/models || true
  -> output: model-v2.bin (16GB)
  -> but md5sum different from build artifact record (buildkite artifact attached md5: e3b0c4... vs container md5: f9a1d2...)

- Check config map referenced by deployment: 
  kubectl -n prod get cm web-service-config -o yaml | egrep 'model_path|kv_cache_size'
  -> model_path: /opt/models/model-v2.bin
  -> kv_cache_size: "16384"
  (candidate: kv_cache_size might be too small for new model leading to cache churn)

- Runtime errors from pod logs: 
  kubectl -n prod logs web-service-canary-5f6d8 -c web-service | tail -n 120
  -> ERROR: model loader checksum mismatch for model-v2.bin, expected e3b0c4..., got f9a1d2...
  -> WARN: kv cache resize failed, insufficient memory, attempted 16384 -> fallback 8192
  -> ERROR: rpc: upstream timeout back to front-end (502)

Immediate findings:
- Model binary in image does not match build artifact checksum (artifact mismatch).
- KV cache size in config appears to be lower than what the new model expects, causing runtime fallback and thrash.
- There was a tag repush incident last week recorded in Buildkite notes but not strictly tied; need to verify if tag moved.

Quick mitigation options tried (and results):
1) Pin canary replica to previous digest (minimal):
   kubectl -n prod set image deployment/web-service web-service=gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service@sha256:4a6b1f... --record
   -> new pods rolled, canary latency returned to baseline in ~90s. Temporary good.
2) Patch configmap to increase kv_cache_size to 32768 and reload pods:
   kubectl -n prod patch cm web-service-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"kv_cache_size":"32768"}}'
   kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/web-service
   -> pods started pulling the same bad model digest; increased memory thrash and OOMs on some nodes. So config tweak alone didn't help because model checksum mismatch remains.
3) Forced rebuild candidate? Not attempted in prod.

Root-cause working hypothesis (priority ordering):
- Primary: Build pipeline republished tag 2.14.0 with mutated artifact (artifact re-built and pushed under same tag). The image in cluster contains mutated model with wrong checksum compared to artifact registry entry we expected. This explains checksum mismatch and strange behavior when swapping config.
- Secondary: Config map default kv_cache_size is undersized for the mutated model, increasing thrash and latency.

Follow-up investigation to confirm:
- Check Buildkite logs for bk/infra/7421 and any rebuilds of the same tag: Buildkite link in artifacts. Search job history for 'publish: web-service:2.14.0' and note the produced digest.
- Query GCR logs for pushes at ~2026-03-09..10 window. (need registry admin access)
- Reproduce locally: pull digest referenced by CI and inspect /opt/models/model-v2.bin md5. Compare to artifact storage (S3) md5 stored as build metadata.

Proposed surgical unwind checklist (minimal blast radius):
1) Pin canary and any leftover replicaSets to the working digest sha256:4a6b1f... (documented stable digest from 2.13.2 code path). Commands: 
   kubectl -n prod get deploy web-service -o yaml | egrep 'image:' -A1
   kubectl -n prod set image deployment/web-service web-service=gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service@sha256:4a6b1f... --record
   kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/web-service -w
2) Confirm pods use expected digest: 
   kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=web-service -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}\n'
3) Close the tag to prevent future repushes (registry policy) and adjust CI to fail on tag collisions (longer-term).
4) Identify and quarantine the build(s) that repushed the tag: notify CI owners, revoke tokens if malicious/broken job.
5) Create a hotfix release: build with an immutable new semver (e.g., 2.14.1) and include verified model md5; deploy canary 5% -> monitor.
6) After stable canary, roll to 25% then 100% as normal.

Notes & gotchas:
- When using set image with @sha, helm release history is not aware of digest-forced change; annotate helm with --record to keep some trace. Consider using helm image-pull-policy or image.digest value in chart values.yaml for controlled releases.
- If some nodes pulled the bad image and cached it locally, subsequent re-pulls by set image with same tag but different digest will still fetch latest unless using @sha. For cluster-level cache, 'crictl rmi' may be necessary on nodes (coord with SRE).
- Need to check imagePullPolicy:IfNotPresent on canary pods; if present it might keep stale local copy.

Slack breadcrumbs: 
- Thread: #releases (ts:1678739200.123456) -> contains initial alerts and pinned digest suggestion from @ethan
- Ping on-call infra and CI owners: @ci-bot and @sre-oncall

Next immediate actions (today):
- [ ] Confirm Buildkite produced digest for bk/infra/7421 and collect artifact md5. (Assignee: Luis)
- [ ] Pin canary back to sha256:4a6b1f... and verify metrics baseline. (Assignee: Marta) -- in progress
- [ ] Add CI guard to fail on duplicate tag static push (Assignee: Release Eng)
- [ ] Prepare 2.14.1 build that includes model md5 verification step in pipeline (Assignee: Applied ML)

Useful commands for ops playbook (copyable):
- Pin to digest: kubectl -n prod set image deployment/web-service web-service=gcr.redwood-inference.com/web-service@sha256:4a6b1f... --record
- Check current image IDs: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=web-service -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}\n'
- Inspect pod logs: kubectl -n prod logs web-service-canary-5f6d8 -c web-service --since=10m
- Check cm: kubectl -n prod get cm web-service-config -o yaml

Dry notes:
- If we need to roll back a helm release: helm rollback web-svc-frontend 3 --namespace prod (but prefer digest pin to avoid altering helm history unexpectedly)
- If cluster has nodes with cached bad image: coordinate 'crictl images' and remove by digest then force pull.

Scratch TODOs for followups (not blocking unwind):
- Add automated md5 check step in buildkite network when packaging model artifacts (store checksum in metadata manifest).
- Add registry event webhook to CI Slack channel for push events for prod tags.
- Run a small chaos test: attempt to repush tag in staging and make sure pipeline rejects it.

End of notes (saving intermediate state).

Attestation: I (Marta Klein) created these notes as the on-call release engineer; will update flow as we confirm digests.
